title: Jeera Rice (Cumin Rice)
tagline: Fluffy basmati tempered with toasted cumin — the perfect everyday side.
intro: Jeera rice is one of the simplest and most useful dishes in the Indian kitchen: fluffy basmati fragrant with toasted cumin seeds and a little ghee. It takes minutes, uses a handful of ingredients, and turns any curry into a complete meal — which is exactly why it appears on menus everywhere.

items: 400 g (2 cups) basmati rice, soaked 20 min

method: Heat the ghee and add the cumin seeds; let them sizzle and turn fragrant (don't burn).
Add the bay leaf and optional whole spices.
Add the drained rice and stir gently to coat in the ghee.
Add the water and salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low until absorbed, 12–15 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and garnish with coriander.
tips: Toasting the cumin properly is the whole flavour of the dish — give it a moment.
Soaking basmati first gives longer, separate grains.
toServe: Pairs with dal, butter chicken or any curry.
